main_text.p: Omnino perfectionem amœnitatis huius instituit Deus: amœnitate facit odoramentorum communio, communionem charitas, quæ perfectionis vinculum à Paulo dicitur: pax necessarium est charitatis instrumentum. c

Quid ergo putamus, miseri? quid fingimus, cùm tanto supercilio alij alios quasi furcilla extrudimus, & censoriam quandam virgulam in hos, in illos promiscuè adhibemus, tanquam si nobis solùm esset iudicij nasus; aut Christus hanc facultatem cessisset nobis, qua ad libidinem animi nostri abutamur? Id sanè faciant Satanæ stabularij: at oues Christi non decet, pastores minimè. Quin potiùs Christo cedimus, nos & illos in communionem corporis & Spiritus sui gratiosissimè adhibenti? Quin potiùs odores amœnissimos ab illo in nos deriuantem manu ipsius animaduertimus? quin potiùs unguento illo odoratissimo fratres communiter nobiscum sentimus delibutos? quin potiùs etiam amicos ad participationem suauissimi eiusdem odoris ab illo capite in corpus unum adscitum iri confidimus? quin potiùs & continendis iis qui iam vocati sunt, & vocandis qui abfunt, damus operam diligentissimè; ab omni fœtore abstinentes, quo crepant animi nostri, & omnem suauissimum odorem illis exhibentes, qui ad Christum & ad nos per Christum unà perducantur? O beatum studium eorum, qui in hoc pietatis officio con-fumunt

page.notes: The printed page is a single text column with page number 200 and running head EIRENICI at the top. The word "confumunt" is broken at the line end as "con-" / "fumunt", and is written here with its printed hyphen. Long s has been transcribed as s throughout. Forms such as "fi" (si), "folùm" (solùm) and "effet" (esset) are read as shown on the scan, but the long-s letters are less clear at this resolution, so they are open to doubt. Small marks at the right edge of the scan are show-through or the book edge and are not transcribed.
